question: There is no pharmacological treatment that improves the core cognitive deficits of intellectual disability; management is entirely based on early intervention, education, therapy, and family support.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. No medication improves intellectual ability per se in intellectual disability. The management framework is non-pharmacological: early intervention services, special needs education (RTE 2009 in India), speech-language therapy, occupational therapy, and family counselling. Drugs are used only for specific comorbidities (epilepsy, hyperactivity, mood disorders), not for the cognitive deficit itself.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. No drug reverses the underlying cognitive deficit in intellectual disability. Pharmacotherapy has a narrow, specific role: treating associated comorbidities (epilepsy, ADHD, anxiety, mood disorders, self-injurious behaviours). The mainstay of management is early developmental intervention — special education, speech therapy, occupational therapy, physiotherapy, and family support. Early intervention in the first 3 years of life maximises developmental plasticity and functional outcomes.
